ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the line $y=kx+b\ (k<0)$ intersects the y-axis at point A and intersects the x-axis at point B, and $(AB+OA)(AB-OA)=\frac{9}{4}$. What is the solution set of the inequality $kx+b>0$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:}\\
Since $(AB+OA)(AB−OA)=\frac{9}{4}$,\\
it follows that $AB^{2}−OA^{2}=\frac{9}{4}$,\\
therefore $OB^{2}=\frac{9}{4}$,\\
hence $OB=\frac{3}{2}$,\\
therefore, the solution set of the inequality $kx+b>0$ is $\boxed{x<\frac{3}{2}}$.
